Definitely got the controller, because I wanted a controller (damn certain games cough dark souls cough for being unplayable without one) and didn't want to get a microsoft or sony one. Haven't had the opportunity to use it yet, however -- I'll give a report when I've messed around with it a bit.
I really want the controller. I'll be waiting for your report.

Okay Primary response -- It seems to work well for a decent range of games. So far I've tried it for three games -- Osmos, Gauntlet, and Borderlands, the Pre-sequel. I also attempted to use it for Drunken Robot Pornography and Rogue Legacy.

Before we start, here are some general comments -- haptic control thing is weird -- It's definitely takes some learning and getting used to. However, it did offer the level of accuracy they promised one I'd used it for a few minutes. I wouldn't play Dota 2 with it, but it worked well enough with shooters and non-shooters for me to enjoy it. It also worked well enough at navigating the desktop that I was perfectly happy using the controller to get a round the page rather than switching back to the mouse for the brief interludes between games where I left steam big picture.

As for reports on how well it played different games:

Osmos is a game where you use your mouse to point a direction, then hit key buttons to spead up/slow down time and move around using your own mass to propell you. It also doesn't come with built-in controller support, being originally designed completely for mouse and keys.

For the game, the controller worked great. Setting up the controls was easy due to the 'community' layout patterns. To explain, users can upload their button patterns for a game to steam, which you can grab to just start playing, which made jumping into the game fairly easy.

The reason I mentioned I attempted Rogue Legacy and Drunken Robot Pornography is because of issues getting the controller set up. Both these games by default are setup to work out of the box with xbox controllers. However, there were issues I had getting it to recognize the controller input for these two games, and I just haven't gotten around to resolving them yet.

That said, both Borderlands and Gauntlet also defaulted with being usable by a controller, and they worked perfectly. Gauntlet was extremely well setup for the controller, and I had zero issues playing that. Borderlands -- lets say aiming was a challenge for about the first half hour of play, before I got the hang of it and could hit what I was aiming for. Little bit later, and I was shooting away perfectly fine.

Some complaints -- handholds are different from what I was used to, making them soar (just minorly, however -- I'm sure after using it for a week I'll be fine), and the haptic feedback thing has some weird behavior when your thumb gets near the edge (it'll backtrack a bit if you go off the side slowly -- going quickly will send you spinning, which was nice). It was also noticeably loud. I'd forget the sound when playing a game, but it'd notice it between games.

There are a few games I'll use it for, where a controller really is better than a mouse and keyboard, but for most my games I'll still being using a mouse and a keyboard.

TL:DR -- so far so good -- issues setting up controller for some games which were set up for controllers, and takes some getting used to.
You sir, have sold me on it. I will be buying one soon. Thanks for the run down by the way

As an addition, I figured out the controller problem I had with Rogue Legacy and Drunken Robot Pornography -- The games will get confused if you turn on the controller before big picture mode. Not sure why, but entering big picture mode, then turning on the controller, fixed the problem.
